## Basic corpus workflow

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)

documents <- df |>
  transmute(
    document_id,
    corpus,
    text = text |>
      stringr::str_replace_all("[[:space:]]+", " ") |>
      stringr::str_squish()
  )

tokens <- documents |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text) |>
  anti_join(get_stopwords(language = "en"), by = "word")

word_counts <- tokens |> count(corpus, word, sort = TRUE)
```

### Python

```python
import re

import pandas as pd

documents = df[["document_id", "corpus", "text"]].copy()
documents["text"] = documents["text"].fillna("").map(
    lambda text: re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
)

tokens = (
    documents.assign(word=documents["text"].str.lower().str.findall(r"\b[^\W\d_]+\b"))
    .explode("word")
    .dropna(subset=["word"])
)

stopwords = {"a", "an", "and", "of", "the", "to"}  # Replace for the corpus language.
tokens = tokens.loc[~tokens["word"].isin(stopwords)]
word_counts = tokens.value_counts(["corpus", "word"]).rename("n").reset_index()
```
::::

Normalization choices are analytical choices. Preserve the original text and do not remove punctuation, case, accents or stopwords until the task calls for it.

## N-grams and concordances

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
bigrams <- documents |>
  unnest_tokens(bigram, text, token = "ngrams", n = 2) |>
  count(corpus, bigram, sort = TRUE)

concordance <- documents |>
  filter(str_detect(text, regex("climate", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  transmute(
    document_id,
    context = str_extract(text, regex(".{0,60}climate.{0,60}", ignore_case = TRUE))
  )
```

### Python

```python
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer

vectorizer = CountVectorizer(ngram_range=(2, 2), min_df=2)
matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform(documents["text"])
bigram_counts = pd.Series(
    matrix.sum(axis=0).A1,
    index=vectorizer.get_feature_names_out(),
).sort_values(ascending=False)

pattern = re.compile(r".{0,60}climate.{0,60}", flags=re.IGNORECASE)
concordance = documents.assign(
    context=documents["text"].map(lambda text: pattern.findall(text))
).explode("context").dropna(subset=["context"])
```

## TF-IDF and corpus comparison

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
tf_idf <- word_counts |>
  bind_tf_idf(term = word, document = corpus, n = n) |>
  arrange(corpus, desc(tf_idf))

comparison <- word_counts |>
  group_by(corpus) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(corpus, word, share) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = corpus, values_from = share, values_fill = 0)
```

### Python

```python
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

corpus_text = documents.groupby("corpus")["text"].agg(" ".join)
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(stop_words="english")
matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform(corpus_text)

tf_idf = pd.DataFrame(
    matrix.toarray(),
    index=corpus_text.index,
    columns=vectorizer.get_feature_names_out(),
).T

comparison = (
    word_counts.assign(
        share=lambda x: x["n"] / x.groupby("corpus")["n"].transform("sum")
    )
    .pivot(index="word", columns="corpus", values="share")
    .fillna(0)
)
```

## Advanced NLP

### Sentiment

Dictionary sentiment is sensitive to language, negation, sarcasm and domain. Inspect matched words and unmatched coverage instead of treating a score as ground truth.

```r
sentiment <- tokens |>
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = "word") |>
  count(document_id, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(score = positive - negative)
```

### Named entity recognition

Use a language-appropriate trained model and inspect errors on a sample of the actual corpus.

```python
import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
entities = [
    {
        "document_id": row.document_id,
        "entity": entity.text,
        "label": entity.label_,
    }
    for row in documents.itertuples()
    for entity in nlp(row.text).ents
]
entities = pd.DataFrame(entities)
```
